en.title: University life
en.summary: Lectures, seminars, essays and student accommodation.

paragraphs: University life has its own routines and its own language. This lesson introduces the main words and lets you practise the present perfect with already, yet and for.
Nina is visiting her friend Omar, who studies at the University of Exeter.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: It's hard but interesting. I have lectures in the morning and seminars in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: No, I share a flat with two friends. We have lived there since September.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: And when is your essay due?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Next Friday. I haven't started it yet, but I've already read most of the books.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: How long is it supposed to be?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Two thousand words. I need to be in the library most of this week.

paragraphs: **1. Already and not yet with the present perfect.** Already shows that something is complete, and not yet that it is still to do. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

blocks.html:
WordExample
alreadyI have already read the books.
not yetI haven't started the essay yet.
forWe have lived here for six months.
sinceWe have lived here since September.

paragraphs: **2. Be due and be supposed to describe deadlines and expectations.** See Introduction to Grammar: Present tense, being and having.

blocks.html:
FormExample
be dueThe essay is due on Friday.
be supposed toIt is supposed to be 2,000 words long.
hand inHand in your work on time.
extensionHe asked for an extension.

items: A lecture has one speaker; a seminar is a discussion in a small group.
Campus is the university grounds; halls of residence are the university-owned accommodation.
A degree is the qualification you receive after studying.
A tutor helps and advises students.

paragraphs: Many British students leave home to study, living in halls of residence in the first year and in shared houses later. In the United States students often live on campus for all four years.
